meta.paper: Cospectral periodic graphs: the spectrum does not determine the graph
meta.author: Jiaqi Yu (Tongji University)
meta.generated: independent reproduction specification; no code distributed with this file
meta.standing_rule: No numerical output is used as a proof: every statement is proved in the text (paper section 5). Numerical checks are cross-validation and counterexample search only.
missing_paper_artifacts: code/spec_K_proof.py (mentioned in paper section 5; not available in this workspace and deliberately not imitated)

definitions.name: V_K and K(m)
definitions.text: V_K = { x in Z^m : sum_i x_i in {0,1} }; K(m) has vertex set V_K with x adjacent to y iff y = x +- e_i for some i.

definitions.name: coroot lattice Q^vee
definitions.text: Q^vee = { x in Z^m : sum_i x_i = 0 } isomorphic to Z^(m-1); identified with Z^(m-1) by x -> (x_1,...,x_(m-1)); characters chi in T^(m-1), z_i = chi(e_i).

definitions.name: affine Weyl group W_a
definitions.text: W_a(A~_(m-1)) = Q^vee semidirect S_m acting by x -> w(x) + lambda; group law (w,lambda)(v,mu) = (wv, lambda + w(mu)) (paper section 5). The S_m action used in w(mu) must be the same convention as in x -> w(x); otherwise the law is not associative.

definitions.name: simple and affine reflections
definitions.text: s_1..s_(m-1) are the simple reflections of the finite Weyl group; s_0 = the affine reflection for theta = e_1 - e_m, and s_theta is the transposition of coordinates 1 and m. The extracted text renders the s_0 formula ambiguously as 's0 = stheta, theta'. Inferred standard normalization: s_0 = (w_0, theta) with w_0 = transposition (1 m). SIGN OF theta is harmless (automorphism psi(w,lambda) = (w,-lambda) fixes all s_i); DROPPING the translation is not harmless.

definitions.name: chamber graph S~_m
definitions.text: S~_m = Cay(W_a, {s_0, s_1, ..., s_(m-1)}); two chambers adjacent iff they share a wall. Left/right Cayley convention unspecified; g -> g^(-1) makes them isomorphic, so girth is unaffected.

definitions.name: periodic graph and periodic rank
definitions.text: X locally finite, connected, simple; Gamma <= Aut(X) free abelian acting freely with finitely many orbits; rank Gamma is the periodic rank.

definitions.name: Floquet spectrum
definitions.text: Spec X = union over chi in T^d of Spec A_chi, where A_chi is indexed by the cell V(X/Gamma) and the entry from the class of x to the class of y is the sum of chi(lambda) over all lambda and all adjacencies x ~ y + lambda inducing that class-to-class transition. The cell is a multigraph.

definitions.name: cell and Floquet matrix of K(m)
definitions.text: A_a = (a_1,...,a_(m-1), -sum a_i); B_b = (b_1,...,b_(m-1), 1 - sum b_i); edges A_a ~ B_(a+e_i), A_a ~ B_a, B_b ~ A_(b-e_i), B_b ~ A_b; the cell is two vertices with m parallel edges of voltages 0, e_1,...,e_(m-1); A_chi = [[0,S],[S,0]] with S(chi) = 1 + z_1 + ... + z_(m-1) (the lower entry is the conjugate, as the paper's proof text states); Spec A_chi = { +- |S(chi)| }.

definitions.name: sublattice Lambda = m Q^vee
definitions.text: Q^vee is the maximal period lattice; Lambda = m Q^vee = { m v : sum_i v_i = 0 } has index m^(m-1) in Q^vee and gives a cell with 2 m^(m-1) vertices, classes indexed by (x_1,...,x_(m-1)) mod m and by sum_i x_i in {0,1}, and a Floquet matrix of that size. The paper gives no explicit Floquet matrix for this cell.

definitions.name: bipartition of K(m)
definitions.text: Every edge joins an A-vertex to a B-vertex; the parts are {sum x_i = 0} = {A_a} and {sum x_i = 1} = {B_b}.

definitions.name: not defined in the paper
definitions.text: The paper gives no formal definition of girth (standard: length of a shortest cycle); no cell/voltage data for S~_m (section 6 states only that its cell has m! vertices); no grid resolution, no box radius for the K(m) BFS, no parameterization of the 60-point character grid of Remark 3.3.

claims.statement: Theorem 1.3: for every m >= 3, Spec K(m) = [-m, m], where the spectrum of a periodic graph is the closure of the union of the spectra of its Floquet matrices over the dual torus (eq. (2)).

expected.endpoints_at_identity_character: cell matrix [[0,m],[m,0]] gives exactly -m and +m; lambda_max must equal the degree m
expected.S_upper_bound: |S(chi)| <= m for all chi, with equality iff z_1 = ... = z_(m-1) = 1 (triangle inequality)

S_zero_witness.m>=4: z_1 = -1 and z_2..z_(m-1) run over all (m-2)-th roots of unity; S(chi) = 0

expected.observed_2026_baseline: explicit witnesses give |S| <= 3.2e-16; on the natural 60-point grid min |S| = 0.000000 and max |S| = m for m = 3,4,5

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.1 and section 5.2: channel 1 (2x2 cell over Q^vee), channel 2 (Lambda-cell of order 2 m^(m-1) built from section 5.1), channel 3 (decidable lift identity Spec A_chi^Lambda = { +- |S((theta+k)/m)| }), criteria G1-G4
claims.tolerance: eigenvalue and algebraic-point comparisons atol 1e-9; fill test is a discrete criterion maxgap <= 2*eps_Lip with eps_Lip = (m-1)*pi/N (no floating-point proxy for the interval equality)
claims.note: The interval equality additionally needs the connectivity of |S(T^(m-1))| plus the two endpoints; that part is proof-only (see C19). Numerics support, never prove.

claims.statement: Theorem 1.4 (K(m) part): girth K(m) = 6 for every m >= 3.

expected.box_certificate: mu_3 = 6 <= 2*3 so the ball of radius 3 certifies the answer (REPRO-SPEC section 4.10 lemma)
expected.observed_2026_baseline: K(3), K(4), K(5): no cycle in the radius-2 ball; mu_3 = mu_4 = 6

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.3: BFS ball of radius r in K(m), girth of the induced finite subgraph equals mu_r, apply mu_r <= 2r; plus exhaustive closed-walk check of length <= 6 from the origin and verification of the two explicit 6-cycles
claims.tolerance: exact integers; vertex adjacency verified exactly; certificate inequality mu_r <= 2r is exact
claims.note: Report (r, mu_r) pairs; a bare in-ball minimum cycle length is only an upper bound and is not accepted.

claims.statement: Theorem 1.4 (chamber part): girth S~_3 = 6, and girth S~_m = 4 for every m >= 4.

expected.structural: for m >= 4 the non-adjacent Coxeter nodes s_1 and s_3 commute, giving the 4-cycle 1, s_1, s_1 s_3, s_3; for m = 3 the type A~_2 Coxeter graph is a triangle, no commuting pair exists, the sign character forces even closed-walk lengths, and the rank-two parabolic <s_i,s_j> = S_3 gives a 6-cycle
expected.observed_2026_baseline: word-metric balls |B_2| = 10/15/21 for m = 3/4/5; mu_3 = 6 (m=3, certificate 6 <= 6), mu_2 = 4 (m=4,5, certificate 4 <= 4)

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.4: chamber ball in the Coxeter word metric via the (w, lambda) realization with the paper's group law, girth of the induced finite subgraph, box certificate mu_r <= 2r; plus group self-tests (involutions, associativity, inverse formula, braid relations) and explicit verification of the braid 6-cycle and the commuting-pair 4-cycle
claims.tolerance: exact; group self-tests are exact equality tests
claims.note: The sign of theta in s_0 is harmless; dropping the translation is not (that error yields girth 4 for m = 3, contradicting the theorem).

claims.statement: Theorem 1.5: for m in {4,5}, K(m) and S~_m are both m-regular, infinite, vertex-transitive, of periodic rank m-1, with Spec K(m) = [-m,m] = Spec S~_m, but girth K(m) = 6 != 4 = girth S~_m; hence they are not isomorphic and the spectrum does not determine the graph.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.4: combine the C01/C24 checks, the C02 and C03 girth certificates, and the quoted input C05
claims.note: Half of the input (Spec S~_m) is quoted from [6, Thm. 6.5] and cannot be independently proved here; see C05 and REPRO-SPEC section 6(a).

claims.statement: Remark 1.6 (quoted): Spec S~_m = [-m, m] for 3 <= m <= 5, taken from the companion book [6, Thm. 6.5].

expected.corroboration_only: sampled chamber-cell Floquet eigenvalues must satisfy |lambda| <= m and approach the endpoints; no counterexample may be found

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.6 (floquet_cell_chamber): cell = S_m with m! vertices, edges w - w s_i with voltage 0 and w - w w_0 with voltage w(theta); diagonalize on a character grid; counterexample search only
claims.tolerance: counterexample search: assert |lambda| <= m + 1e-9; NO positive verification tolerance exists for this quoted claim
claims.note: 2026 baseline (chamber cell): m=3 (6x6, 3600 characters) all |lambda| <= 3 with min |lambda| = 0 and largest positive-eigenvalue gap 0.120; m=4 (24x24, 512 characters) all |lambda| <= 4 with min |lambda| = 0, gap 0.077; m=5 (120x120, 60 random characters) max 4.972 <= 5. This is an absence of counterexamples, not a verification. Full bibliographic data of [6] is not given by the paper.

claims.statement: Remark 1.6 (quoted): for m >= 6 the companion book [6] proves the inclusion Spec S~_m is a subset of [-m, m] and the two endpoints +-m.

expected.inclusion: Spec S~_m subset of [-m, m] for m >= 6

claims.method: quoted; only a counterexample search against the inclusion is possible
claims.note: Cannot be checked independently without access to [6].

claims.statement: Open problem/section 6: for m >= 6 the equality Spec S~_m = [-m, m] is open; closing it would extend Theorem 1.5 to all m >= 4.

expected.obstruction: the cell of S~_m has m! vertices against 2 for K(m); for K(m) the equality reduces to |S(chi)| attaining 0 (explicit witness), whereas for S~_m one must show two branches meet, with no explicit witness available

claims.method: no computational acceptance test; record as open
claims.note: Do not report any numerical result as settling this.

claims.statement: Remark 1.7: any identification that uses only the spectrum as a set (in particular lambda_max, lambda_min, or the statement that the spectrum is an interval) assigns the same value to K(m) and S~_m and therefore cannot separate them. The paper does NOT claim that no spectral invariant can.

expected.scope_caveat: finer data such as the spectral measure or the density of states may well distinguish the pair

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.9; check equality of the two endpoints and of the interval; the logical statement itself is proof-only
claims.tolerance: endpoint comparison atol 1e-9; the implication is not numerically verifiable
claims.note: Numerics can only confirm that the three listed coarse invariants agree.

claims.statement: Remark 1.7 and section 6: whether finer spectral data (spectral measure, density of states) also agree for the pair is left open; the computations of section 5 do not settle it.
claims.method: no acceptance test; record as open
claims.note: Do not claim the density of states agrees or disagrees.

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.5: direct pointwise verification, plus the second 6-cycle pattern of the section 4 proof: x, x+e_1, x+e_1-e_2, x+e_1-e_2+e_3, x-e_2+e_3, x+e_3, x
claims.note: The second pattern uses only e_1, e_2, e_3, hence applies to every m >= 3.

claims.statement: Example 1.8: a 4-cycle in S~_4 is 1, s_1, s_1 s_3, s_3 (nodes 1 and 3 are not adjacent in the Coxeter cycle of type A~_3, so s_1 and s_3 commute); the pair s_1, s_2 would not do because adjacent nodes do not commute.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.4 group arithmetic: verify s_1 s_3 = s_3 s_1 and s_1 s_3 not in {1, s_1, s_3}; verify s_1 s_2 != s_2 s_1 (they satisfy the braid relation (s_1 s_2)^3 = 1)
claims.note: Verified in the 2026 baseline for m = 4 and m = 5.

claims.statement: Lemma 2.2: K(m) is Q^vee-periodic of rank m-1 with exactly two orbits on V_K, namely {sum_i x_i = 0} and {sum_i x_i = 1}; S~_m is Q^vee-periodic of rank m-1 with |W_a / Q^vee| = m!.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.6: for a fixed level, map x -> x' by lambda = x' - x and verify lambda is in Q^vee exactly when the levels agree; count the coset representatives (w,0) of Q^vee in W_a, which are in bijection with S_m
claims.note: The word exactly (no other orbits) is a statement about all of V_K; the numerical check verifies the two-level structure on representatives plus the arithmetic criterion.

claims.statement: Lemma 2.2: both K(m) and S~_m are m-regular, infinite, locally finite and vertex-transitive.

expected.regularity: every vertex has exactly m neighbours
expected.vertex_transitive: K(m) via x -> x + lambda (lambda in Q^vee); S~_m is a Cayley graph

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.6: count the m neighbours from the edge list (5) for a vertex of each level; verify x -> x + lambda is an automorphism by the voltage bookkeeping of section 5.1
claims.note: Vertex-transitivity of K(m) is also what licenses the single-ball girth certificate of REPRO-SPEC section 4.10.

claims.statement: Remark 2.3: a lattice can serve as a period lattice only if it preserves V_K, which already forces it into Q^vee; so Q^vee is the maximal period lattice and every other legitimate choice is a sublattice Lambda of finite index. Lambda = m Q^vee has index m^(m-1) in Q^vee and gives a cell with 2 m^(m-1) vertices, the classes being indexed by (x_1,...,x_(m-1)) mod m and by sum_i x_i in {0,1}; the Floquet matrix has that size.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.1: enumerate classes algebraically as (a mod m, level); build edges from (a,0) to (a + e_j mod m, 1) for j < m and to (a,1), with wrap-around voltages in m Q^vee
claims.note: TRAP: enumerating V_K inside a coordinate box and reducing mod m undercounts. 2026 baseline: with box [-3,3]^5 for m = 5 the count is 1243, not 1250 (representatives can have last coordinate up to +-16). Use the algebraic enumeration.

claims.statement: Proposition 2.5 (quoted from [3,2]): the union in eq. (2) coincides with the spectrum of the adjacency operator A on l^2(V(X)) (Floquet/Bloch decomposition).

expected.identity: Spec X as defined in (2) equals the spectrum of A on l^2(V(X))

claims.method: quoted; the paper gives a short proof; at most a finite-truncation corroboration is possible
claims.tolerance: not applicable for the general operator statement
claims.section: Prop. 2.5; cited to [3] eq. (1.11) and section 7, and [2] section 4
claims.note: The paper appends a sketch proof, but the essential theorem is attributed to [2],[3].

claims.statement: Remark 2.6: Definition 2.4 is phrased for a multigraph cell because a cell can have parallel edges; the Floquet matrices then sum the characters of the several translations realising the same class-to-class transition. For K(m) the cell has two vertices and m parallel edges, so the multigraph formulation is exactly what makes Definition 2.4 apply. K(m) itself is never treated as a multigraph.

expected.parallel_edges: m edges A-B with voltages 0, e_1, ..., e_(m-1)

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.7: count parallel edges and voltages of cell(Q^vee); verify that summing over translations is required by comparing with the simple quotient graph over Lambda
claims.note: The necessity of the multigraph formulation is a proof-level remark; the multigraph fact itself is checkable.

claims.statement: Lemma 3.1: (i) {A_a} and {B_b} are exactly the two Q^vee-orbits in V_K, each in bijection with Z^(m-1) via x -> (x_1,...,x_(m-1)); (ii) the edges of K(m) are exactly those listed in (5); (iii) the cell V_K/Q^vee is a two-vertex graph with m parallel edges of voltages 0, e_1, ..., e_(m-1), and A_chi = [[0,S],[S,0]] with S(chi) = 1 + z_1 + ... + z_(m-1); hence Spec A_chi = { +- |S(chi)| }.

expected.bijection: x -> (x_1,...,x_(m-1)) injective on each level since the last coordinate is determined by the sum
expected.edges: A_a ~ B_(a+e_i) (i<m), A_a ~ B_a, B_b ~ A_(b-e_i) (i<m), B_b ~ A_b

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.7 and section 5.1: verify sum A_a = 0, sum B_b = 1; verify the edge list reproduces exactly the neighbours of each vertex; verify the cell matrix is Hermitian with A = [[0,S],[conj S,0]] and spectrum { +- |S| }
claims.tolerance: exact for combinatorial statements; atol 1e-12 for Hermiticity, 1e-9 for eigenvalues
claims.note: The paper displays S(chi) in both off-diagonal entries; its own proof text says the opposite direction carries the conjugate.

claims.statement: Remark 3.2 and Remark 3.4: every edge of K(m) joins an A-vertex to a B-vertex, so K(m) is bipartite with parts {sum x_i = 0} = {A_a} and {sum x_i = 1} = {B_b}; it is m-regular since each A_a has the m neighbours B_(a+e_1), ..., B_(a+e_(m-1)), B_a and each B_b likewise.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.7: check that each neighbour differs in level; count neighbours
claims.note: Bipartiteness also implies triangle-freeness, which is used in the girth certificate.

claims.statement: Remark 3.3 (topological part): |S(T^(m-1))| is connected because it is the continuous image of the connected torus; this is what rules out a spectral gap, and it is the only place where the topology of the torus is used. The witness for |S| = 0 is explicit at every m, so the endpoint 0 need not be searched numerically.
claims.method: proof-only; numerically one can only sample the image and check the discrete gap criterion G3 (REPRO-SPEC section 4.9) and evaluate the explicit witness exactly
claims.tolerance: not applicable to the connectivity statement; the witness evaluation uses atol 1e-12
claims.note: Do not report the G3 gap test as a proof that the image is an interval.

claims.statement: Remark 3.3 (numerical aside): on a 60-point grid in each angle, the sampled minimum of |S| for m = 4 is about 0.04 rather than 0.

expected.acceptance_role: diagnostic only; must not be used as a pass/fail threshold

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.9 and section 8 table A6: evaluate |S| on theta_i = 2*pi*k/60 and on shifted variants
claims.note: 2026 baseline: on the natural grid (k = 0..59) the minimum is exactly 0.000000 for m = 3,4,5, because the explicit witness z = (-1, 1, -1) for m = 4 lies on the grid; a half-integer-offset grid gives 0.052354; excluding k = 0 gives about 0.105. The paper does not specify the grid parameterization, so 0.04 is not reproducible under any natural reading tested. This does not affect any theorem.

claims.statement: Remark 3.4: the bipartition of K(m) is {A_a} union {B_b} in the notation (3), since every edge changes sum_i x_i by +-1.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.7
claims.note: Same content as C18, kept separate because the paper states it separately.

claims.statement: Remark 3.5: counting both signs +-e_i for each of the 2m directed steps gives S(1) = 2(m-1) + 1 = 2m - 1 and lambda_max = 2m - 1, which is wrong; by (5) the two signs lead to the same edge of the cell, so the cell has one edge per direction and S(1) = m. For m = 4 the false answer is 7 against the true degree 4; the mistake is caught at once by comparing lambda_max with the degree. The other way to get the cell wrong is the choice of the period lattice (Remark 2.3).
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.7: assert S(1) = m and lambda_max = m; assert the neighbour count per direction is one
claims.note: This is the paper's own suggested consistency check and should be implemented as an assertion.

claims.statement: Section 5 (size and regularity): for m = 3, 4, 5 the class count is |V_K / Lambda| = 2 m^(m-1) = 18, 128, 1250 for the sublattice Lambda = m Q^vee of index m^(m-1) in Q^vee, and every vertex has exactly m neighbours.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.1 (algebraic class enumeration and edge construction)
claims.note: 2026 baseline reproduces 18, 128, 1250 by algebraic enumeration.

claims.statement: Section 5 (spectrum check (i)): the identity character gives the adjacency matrix, whose extremes are exactly +-m for m = 3, 4, 5 (to machine precision).
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.2 channel 2 at theta = 0: the Lambda-cell matrix becomes the 0/1 adjacency matrix of the quotient graph; take its extreme eigenvalues
claims.note: 2026 baseline: extremes are exactly -+m for m = 3 and m = 4 with the Lambda-cell matrix (18x18 and 128x128).

claims.statement: Section 5 (spectrum check (ii)): the Floquet matrices are diagonalised on a grid of characters; the sampled eigenvalues stay inside [-m, m], fill it, and a continuous eigenvalue path from chi_0 to a generic character sweeps the whole interval. Neither check is used as a proof: the proof of Theorem 1.3 is the argument of section 3.

expected.fill: discrete gap criterion G3 (maxgap <= 2*eps_Lip with eps_Lip = (m-1)*pi/N) and path criterion G4

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.9 and section 5.2 criteria G1-G4
claims.tolerance: eigenvalue bounds atol 1e-9; fill uses a discrete criterion, never a floating-point approximation of the interval equality
claims.note: The word fill is not defined in the paper; this spec replaces it by the decidable criteria G3/G4 and states explicitly that they only falsify large gaps.

claims.statement: Section 5 (girth, K(m)): BFS in a box gives girth 6 for m = 3, 4, 5.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.3
claims.note: The box radius used in the paper is not stated; this spec fixes r = 3 and certifies it via mu_3 <= 6.

claims.statement: Section 5 (chamber graph): the affine Weyl group is realised as {(w, lambda)} with the group law (w, lambda)(v, mu) = (wv, lambda + w(mu)), the ball of radius 6 is built from the Coxeter presentation, and the girth computed inside it is 6 for m = 3 and 4 for m = 4, 5.
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.4: word-metric ball plus girth of the induced subgraph; the certificate already holds at r = 3 (m = 3) and r = 2 (m >= 4)
claims.tolerance: exact for girth; associativity and involution self-tests are exact
claims.note: 2026 baseline ball sizes are for the consistent convention (pq)(i) = q(p(i)) with (w.x)_i = x_(w(i)); an inconsistent pairing gives 114, 547, 1292 for the radius-6 balls while still returning girth 6/4/4, so ball size is a useful diagnostic but girth alone does not validate the group law.

claims.statement: Section 5 (non-isomorphism): same degree and different girth for m = 4 (6 versus 4) and m = 5 (6 versus 4).
claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 4.4; combine C02, C03, C13
claims.note: No numerical output is used as a proof (paper section 5, closing sentence).

claims.statement: Section 6 (the gap at m >= 6): Spec S~_m = [-m, m] is known for 3 <= m <= 5; for m >= 6 only the inclusion into [-m, m] and the two endpoints are proved; closing the gap would extend Theorem 1.5 to all m >= 4. The obstruction: the cell of S~_m has m! vertices, that of K(m) two; for K(m) the Floquet matrix is 2x2 and the equality reduces to |S(chi)| attaining 0, which has an explicit witness, whereas for S~_m one must show that two branches meet, with no explicit witness available.

expected.obstruction: branch crossing without explicit witness; cell size m! against 2

claims.method: no acceptance test; record as open. Numerically one may only search for counterexamples to the inclusion
claims.note: The explanation of the obstruction is proof-level.

claims.statement: Section 6 (other invariants): degree, periodic rank, the two spectral endpoints and bipartiteness all agree for the pair, so none of them can identify it; whether finer spectral data such as the density of states also agree is left open; it would be interesting to know the smallest metric invariant that does separate them, and whether the pair can be separated by a finite computation on the cell (the answer is yes if and only if the two cells are not isomorphic as voltage graphs).

expected.finite_cell_computation: yes if and only if the two cells are not isomorphic as voltage graphs

claims.method: REPRO-SPEC section 5.5 (quotient_isomorphism_check): the two cells have 2 vertices (K(m)) and m! vertices (S~_m), so for m >= 4 they are trivially non-isomorphic as voltage graphs
claims.tolerance: exact vertex counts; voltage-graph isomorphism search is exact (only needed when the vertex counts agree)
claims.note: Inference: because the cell sizes differ (2 versus m!) for every m >= 4, the paper's iff-criterion is trivially satisfied in the range m = 4,5 actually used, so it carries no additional information there. The voltage data of the chamber cell is not given by the paper; REPRO-SPEC section 5.6 supplies an inference plus numerical corroboration.

claims.statement: Section 6 (cospectrality in wider families): the same mechanism - a Floquet matrix whose spectrum is +- |S(chi)| with |S| sweeping an interval - produces cospectral graphs whenever two periodic graphs of the same degree have the same interval but different local structure. The pair here is the smallest instance the author knows in this root-system family.

expected.mechanism: Floquet spectrum +- |S(chi)| with |S| sweeping an interval
expected.smallest_known_instance: the pair for m = 4,5 in this root-system family

claims.method: proof-only; the paper constructs no further family
claims.note: No additional examples are given in the paper.

claims.statement: Section 6 (prior art): isospectrality is classical for finite graphs and known in the periodic setting for operators - Floquet-isospectral Schrodinger operators on periodic graphs exist [4], with the strongest recent statement being the construction of a periodic potential Floquet-isospectral to the zero potential [5]. Those results concern operators Delta + Q on a fixed graph; the statement here is of a different kind because the two graphs are different and are distinguished by the girth. The author has not found a printed pair of vertex-transitive periodic graphs cospectral for the reasons exhibited here.

prior_art: [4] W. Liu, Floquet isospectrality for periodic graph operators, JDE 374 (2023)
[5] M. Faust, J. Liu, et al., arXiv:2401.09731 (2024)
expected.distinction: different graphs, not an auxiliary potential
expected.literature_claim: no printed pair of vertex-transitive periodic graphs cospectral for the same reason

claims.note: The literature claim cannot be checked from the paper alone.

claims.statement: Section 6 (provenance of the spectrum of S~_m): it is stated as a quoted theorem rather than reproved here, flagged explicitly in Remark 1.6; an independent proof would make Theorem 1.5 self-contained.
